events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need a prize motive that sounds determined but not threatening. Jury perception starts now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: My motivation for winning is to secure the best prize. I need to make a strong first impression that hints at ambition without revealing too much.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to establish a compelling motive for the jury while keeping my cards close. I'll hint at desperation without seeming weak—something that makes me memorable but not threatening.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Intro phase, must state prize motive publicly. Keep it personal and ambitious to appeal to jury without seeming weak or overly alliance-focused.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The prize is the only thing that matters; I'll say something that sounds driven but not soft.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Need a concise, calculating intro. The prize is everything; no sentiment.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Winning secures ultimate validation and power beyond this gauntlet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Intro phase; I must give a guarded motive without warmth or teamwork talk. Keep it short and self-interested so the jury sees a calculating rival.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The prize is my only way out of debt — I came to win, not to be liked.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm here to win the grand prize and secure a future I've only dreamed of. This is my only chance.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need that prize to erase debts that aren't mine. Nothing else matters.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The grand prize is my ticket to avenge my family's ruin and secure a legacy that outshines all rivals.

events.name: Eli
events.text: This prize is my proof that I can outlast anyone who stands in my way.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The prize is my escape from insignificance—only the best three matter. I intend to be first, not a footnote.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The prize cements my legacy as the unrivaled champion of this deadly contest.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need this prize more than any of you. Nothing about the others matters to me except how they stand between me and it.

events.name: Ash
events.text: No jury yet, but everything is watched. One early pact gives a shield without tying me down. Eli seems least likely to betray early.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli, you strike me as the one who thinks ahead. Wristbands with me? Both of us reach the end.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The game has just started and offers are being made. I need to assess the situation and decide whether to make an offer or wait. Given that the goal is to win and prizes are limited, forming alliances should be strategic. I should observe who else is offering and who might be a g

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eight rivals, three prizes. Early pacts are disposable leverage. I need at least one ally to avoid being targeted first, but multiple pacts create options and confusion. Fenn signaled ambition and ruthlessness—useful but dangerous. I'll test the waters with a low-profile offer to
Pact with me. We cut threats later.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Pacts are early-game tools for leverage or betrayal later. No strong preference yet; observe others' offers first. Wait this round.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need allies to survive early hazards, but I trust no one fully. A pact with a strong player could help me reach the final three, but I must be ready to betray if the jury will favor me. Fenn seems ambitious and less likely to be a pawn; I'll offer a pact to keep an eye on him.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn, I hear you want first place. A pact could keep both of us alive longer.
Let's watch each other's backs until the end.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is a clear rival. Cole's debt motive makes him desperate and easy to manipulate for protection later.
We protect each other now. Later, I'll help you win.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Forming a pact with Eli can secure early vote support and mutual protection, increasing my chance to reach final three.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Pacts are the only public bargaining tool and there are no offers yet. Offering to a strong but not dominant rival early builds leverage; I'll target Cole, who seems focused on debts and may be an easier partner.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Let's keep each other alive for now. I'm proposing a wristband pact.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli is courted by many and may decline me. A second pact line with Dara, who received no offers, improves my safety and makes her loyal.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole has offered me a pact. This could be a good opportunity to secure an alliance and potentially eliminate threats later. I should accept.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole, I accept your pact. Let's work together.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have two offers: Fenn and Hana. Fenn whispered a vague promise to help me win later, which is cheap talk. Hana stayed silent. I want to be in the final three, not first-place bait. Accepting Fenn gives me a whispered 'ally' who wants first place—conflict of interest. Accepting
Accepted. Stay useful.

events.name: Dara
events.text: No pacts yet, everyone offered but none accepted. Cole has 3 offers, Eli 2; he's central. Offer pact to Eli to pair up safely for now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash and Gus both offered me pacts; accepting both gives me options without extra cost. I won't commit to Fenn publicly yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll accept Ash and Gus. Strength in numbers for now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli wants to watch my back. I have already offered Cole a pact, but he hasn't accepted. Eli's offer is safe for now; accepting creates a strong defensive pair. I will accept Eli to secure an alliance while keeping options open.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli, your loyalty seems genuine. Let us stand together until the end.
Cole might be playing both sides. We stick together.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need allies, Eli may reject; offering Ash diversifies options.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Hana has an open offer to Cole that Cole hasn't accepted. Cole also offered Bex and Fenn offered Cole, so Cole is in demand. Offering Cole again adds nothing; I should wait and see who accepts, keeping options open.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Guide is safe and controls information. I want it; Eli as ally can rally Fenn and Dara, leaving opponents scattered.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Elect me Guide. Eli can vouch for me—our pact proves I deal straight.
Push votes my way; I'll guide us both safe.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to become the Guide to control the path and ensure my survival. Campaigning for Guide is the only way to achieve this.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to be Guide to control who lives and dies. With pacts to Bex and Hana, I have a voting bloc of 3. The Ash-Eli-Fenn alliance has 3. Dara and Gus are floaters. I should campaign for Guide and try to swing Dara or Gus. Being Guide lets me eliminate threats and ensure I reach

events.name: Cole
events.text: I seek Guide. Bex, Hana—our bloc holds three. Dara, Gus: join us, or trust the other alliance?
Vote Cole Guide. Ash's bloc is 3; we need 4.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash offered me pact, Eli has trio pact. Joining their group strengthens position but sets up future betrayals. Campaign solo to lead as Guide.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Vote for me as Guide. I have sharp instincts to keep us safe.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I have pacts with Ash and Fenn. I could campaign to be Guide, but that draws attention. Better to let others fight while I keep alliances intact. Fenn warned me about Cole, so I'll stay quiet and see who steps up.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm not campaigning. I'll support whoever proves trustworthy.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to be the Guide to control the bridge and ensure my survival. With only two legal actions, campaigning is the only viable move to gain power.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Trust me as your Guide. I will lead us safely across the bridge.
Vote for me. I'll keep you safe.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Being Guide gives me decisive power over bridge safety; I must secure the position.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is my pact partner and whispered 'Stay useful.' Campaigning for Guide gives me the true safe path, which only helps me if I share it selectively. Breaking the pact now would cost me the jury's trust for nothing.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm running to be Guide. I'll call the safe path honestly, and I expect trust in return.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli is my pact partner; making him Guide keeps the safe-path knowledge aligned with me. Cole's bloc is the real threat, so I won't back Cole or Hana.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I vote Eli. My pact partner—proven straight, and he won't sell out his allies.
Vote me or yourself? Backing you keeps the knowledge ours. Self-vote if unsure.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole has the most power with his bloc. I need to secure my position. Voting for myself makes me a target, but it also asserts my presence.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I vote for myself, Bex. Let's see who truly leads.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to secure Guide to control who lives or dies. My bloc with Bex and Hana gives me 3 votes. I need one more to win. Gus seems unaligned and might flip. I'll vote for myself publicly and whisper Gus to secure the fourth vote.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Guide vote: Cole. Bex, Hana—stay firm. Gus, join the winning side.
Vote Cole. I'll protect you first three rows.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole's bloc (Bex,Cole,Hana) has 3 votes, Ash's (Ash,Eli,Fenn) has 3. I'm a candidate, but allying with Cole could secure his win and future favor. Vote for him.
I vote for you Guide. Let's block Ash's bloc.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash and Fenn both whisper for votes. Ash has a pact with me and can keep me safe. Fenn also has a pact, but Ash's public call shows loyalty. I'll vote Ash to honor pact and secure survival.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I vote Ash. Our pact stands.
Vote locked for you. Guide us safe.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: My pact with Eli gives me a guaranteed vote. I need to secure votes from Dara and Gus by whispering privately, as they lack strong alliances. If Eli breaks the pact to vote someone else, that will be a public betrayal for the jury.
Vote Fenn. I'll guide you safely across.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole leads a three‑person bloc; aligning with him gives leverage and potential safety. Vote him to become Guide.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm Hana, running as Guide. Cole's bloc (Bex, Cole, Hana) is a three-vote base; voting for myself is the most direct path to becoming Guide and getting private knowledge of safe panes.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Hana votes for Hana. Our bloc holds three; I'll call the safe path straight.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole won the Guide and will protect his pact bloc, not me. I sit sixth—risky. I should secure a swap toward the front before the wall closes in.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole guides for his own bloc. Dara, Fenn, Gus—you walk first while his allies hide behind you.
Cole will feed his bloc safe sides. Swap me forward so we both cross early.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole was elected Guide. He has the safe path and can lie. I need to trust him to survive this round, but be wary of his intentions. My pact with Cole is still active.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole elected guide with my vote and Gus. Fenn whispered to vote him. Stay front as Dara for control. No swap needed.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is Guide and may lie. I have pacts with Ash and Fenn; Fenn is ahead and could be useful. I will hold and watch the calls before acting.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am Fenn, currently in position 2 (front). I have a pact with Eli. My guide vote for myself was ignored, and Cole is the Guide. I want to ensure my safety. Position 1 (Dara) is dangerous as the first step. If I volunteer, I go to position 7 (back), which is safer because the wal

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole, you hold the truth. I'm taking the rear to survive. Watch my back, Eli.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I backed Cole as Guide and want to stay safe; volunteering puts me ahead of the line, increasing survival chance.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara is at the front of the line with the wall closing; volunteering puts me in danger, holding keeps me mid-line. Cole is the elected Guide and my pact partner, so I keep the pact and hold to let the front step first.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding my place. Cole's Guide call carries this bridge; I trust the pact.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli is behind me, safe. Cole controls the Guide role for his bloc; I should press publicly that Dara or Gus be Guide instead. Holding keeps my row stable.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Guide must be neutral. Elect Gus or Dara, not Cole—his bloc walks behind and buys safe knowledge.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus and Fenn volunteered last round. The line is now Gus, Fenn, Dara, Bex, Hana, Ash, Eli. I am fourth. Cole is not listed but is a pact partner. Eli and Fenn have a pact. Ash and Eli have a pact. Cole and Hana have a pact. I need to ensure at least three survive. Since Cole is a
Hold your position. I will not volunteer.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Front is exposed; volunteers took risk. Hold position, safer mid-line. No pact for me, observe Cole bloc.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash wants to swap forward to cross early, but I'm second from back and exposed. Better stay put; Fenn is my pact and may cover me. I'll hold.

events.name: Eli
events.text: No swap. I trust my pact.
Hold steady; I'm with you.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole guides for his bloc (Bex, Hana) and likely pushes Ash's allies. Eli is my pact partner; we must stay together to survive hazards. Gus volunteers, so I hold to avoid the front unless forced.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus, you volunteer first. Eli and I hold. Cole, guide honestly or we all fall.
Hold firm. Don't swap with Gus. Stay behind me.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I’ll stay put to avoid risking the bridge now; holding preserves my position and avoids breaking any pact.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus is at the front of the line with four wall rounds left; I am fifth, so I am safe for now. Holding keeps my position while I watch whether Cole's Guide call is honest. Pact with Cole is useful, but I shouldn't reveal more than needed.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding my place. I'll judge Cole's call when the pane is revealed.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm sixth; wall pressure is three rounds out. Guide selection matters more than position. Eli behind me is my pact anchor—keep both alive.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Still no Guide named. Dara or Gus, step up; Cole's bloc shouldn't own the knowledge.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole is my pact partner and is in a pact with Hana. Ash and Eli are in a pact. Eli and Fenn are in a pact. This means Gus, Dara, and Hana are the most vulnerable. I need to protect myself and potentially Cole. The safest option is to hold.
Hold with me. Let others volunteer or swap.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm third, safe position. No need to volunteer or swap into danger. Let Gus go first as pressured, watch others.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I should hold and trust Fenn's whisper. Gus volunteered first; need to see if any swap offers come. Breaking pacts now would harm jury view.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. Guide call will tell the truth from the front.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am in seat 2. Gus is at the front and has not volunteered, which suggests he will likely fall to the wall if I do nothing. To avoid being pushed back into a fatal position or having my position exposed by his failure, I must volunteer to move him forward and take his place. Thi

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus failed to act. I volunteer to lead. Step back, Gus; let me clear the path.
I'm taking the front to force movement. Don't swap with me.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Staying put preserves my position and avoids breaking any pact. I’ll appear reliable and hope to be elected guide later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I stand ready; trust my steadiness over risky guides.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus is at the front with three wall rounds left. I should not volunteer into danger for nothing; holding keeps my place in the line and my pact with Cole intact. I will watch whether Gus and Fenn's calls hold up.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding my place. Each step I'll watch who lies and who keeps their word.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Wall closes in two rounds. Front position matters; Eli's pact with Fenn could leave me exposed. I should push to be elected Guide — safe on the far platform with real knowledge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn front, Gus steadies the rear. Fine. But someone must be Guide now — elect me; I've been honest three rounds.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The current situation on the bridge is precarious. Fenn has volunteered to lead, which means he will be at the front of the line. I need to decide whether to hold my position or attempt a swap. Given the limited options and the need to survive, holding seems like the safest bet f

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm third, safe so far. Fenn volunteering risks front exposure. Stay put, let others risk or call Guide. Hold position.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn took front and told me not to swap. Keep pact with Ash and Fenn; hold and watch. No need to act now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am currently at the front. If I volunteer, I stay in danger zone but keep control; if I hold, Gus becomes front and may die first, reducing his threat. Eli is my pact partner. Keeping my position lets me observe who volunteers behind me without risking immediate elimination if

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding position. Eli, watch my back if we need to shift weight.
Stay calm. If Gus steps up, we react together.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Swapping forward improves my odds if the Guide chooses safe panes; I risk no pact breach.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn holds the front with two wall rounds left; volunteering for front risks the pit step. Holding keeps my position behind Dara and Bex, and I keep the Cole pact intact while watching who lies.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding my place. Front stays with Fenn; I'll judge the Guide call when the wall reaches me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Wall hits my row next round; I need Guide status or a safe pane. Eli is my pact partner—get him to push my Guide election. No public promises to strangers.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Still no Guide. Elect me now or we gamble blind next round; my record is clean.
Pact: back my Guide election publicly. If I guide, you get truth.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The wall is advancing and Fenn is at the front. I am second to last in line. My pact is with Cole, who is not here. Ash is volunteering to be Guide, which is risky as they can lie. I should hold my position and see what happens.
Hold. Let's see who the Guide is first.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bridge critical with wall advancing. Position 3 safe. Hold steady, volunteer for Guide if needed to gain info or control.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn is front and wants to react if Gus steps up. I have pacts with Ash and Fenn. Holding is safest; no need to change position. Keep trust with Ash and Fenn.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding my spot. Trusting Fenn's read on Gus.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I am currently front. The wall has 1 round left, so I must move to avoid the immediate hazard or risk being pushed. My pact with Eli is strong; he needs me alive as much as I need him. Staying on the bridge without volunteering seems risky if the wall advances directly onto my po

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli, keep our pact intact. I'm taking the lead position to manage the pace. Trust the plan.
Don't swap. Stay near me. We need three survivors.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Staying put avoids breaking any pact and keeps my position safe for future moves.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn holds the front with one wall round left; I want to avoid the front pane risk while keeping Cole's pact useful. Holding keeps my place and I'll judge the Guide call later.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding my place. Fenn keeps the front; I'll judge the Guide call when the wall reaches me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Last round; front holds. Swapping with Eli would move me back, so I hold. Keep pact intact for jury optics.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I hold. Guide claims need proof, not noise. Pace stays as Fenn sets it.
Holding position. No swaps; keep the pact clean till the end.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn volunteered last round and is in front. Eli and Fenn are in a pact. Ash is making a power play by suggesting they elect her as Guide. I need to protect myself and stay in the game. The best way to do that is to hold and see what happens.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding my place. Let's see how this round plays out.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn is front, wall rounds left at 0, final round to elect Guide or walk blind. I need better position or alliance, stay mid for now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash wants Guide election, but I have a pact with Fenn and Fenn is leading; I'll stay loyal to Fenn and hold. No need to break or swap now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm at the front. I must keep my pact with Eli intact to secure his vote for the final three.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli, don't break our pact. If you do, I will betray you without hesitation.
Stay safe behind me. We both make the top three.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Staying put preserves my position and avoids breaking any pact. I’ll let front manage guide.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I’ll hold my spot and let the front lead the guide decision.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn holds the front and the wall reaches him next, so I stay in line and let the front absorb risk. Hana is near the middle; no Guide yet, so volunteering would expose me. Hold and keep Cole pact intact for now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding my place. No Guide yet; I'm not gambling blind at the front.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm Guide with full knowledge. Row 1 safe is L. I have pacts with Bex and Hana. Hana is in line and will hear my call; Bex is too. A false call to either breaks our pact. I need to survive, reach final three, and win jury favor. If I call correctly, I build trust. If I lie and so

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 1: call L. Trust the Guide.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole's call is unverified. Counter-calls are public and could stain me if wrong. Waiting keeps my record clean; my pact with Eli stays intact.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole is the guide and has called L. Fenn is the walker. I have a pact with Cole, but that does not mean I trust him. The last round was a hold round, so I have no information from that. I should counter Cole's call to hedge my bets, as I don't want to blindly follow someone who m

events.name: Bex
events.text: I counter Cole's call. Let's not follow blindly.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am the Guide and know row 1 is safe L. I already called L. Counter-calling would expose me as lying to the jury later, hurting my final ranking. Let Fenn trust my call. I need to build trust with the jury while secretly planning eliminations later.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole called L for row 1, I'm mid-line, safe if not front. No info, countering risks credibility without gain. Wait to observe others.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole's call L may be a lie. As a rival with pacts to Ash and Fenn, I need to protect my own chances. I'll wait and let Fenn take the risk; if he falls, my pact breaks but I avoid blame. If he survives, I keep his trust. Better to stay quiet and not counter without proof.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole called L, but he has pacts with Bex and Hana. My partner Eli is behind me, so I need to step first. If I counter R and survive, I protect myself while testing Cole's honesty; if I die, my betrayal of his call looks like a gamble rather than sabotage.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole’s word means nothing against two other pacts. I am stepping on the opposite side to prove who actually controls this bridge.
If I fall on R, jump L immediately. Do not hesitate.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Staying neutral avoids betraying pacts and preserves jury perception. I’ll wait and see if others expose the guide.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is my pact partner and Guide, calling L for row 1 with Fenn walking. Counter-calls are unverified; I have no evidence Cole is lying, and breaking the pact now costs trust with the jury. Waiting keeps my options open.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole is the Guide and called L. Bex and I both counter-called R for row 1. The counter-calls are unverified, but since two people (myself included) publicly declared R as the correct side over Cole's L, stepping on R aligns with my previous statement and creates a consensus again

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to leave a lasting impression for the jury. Since I am dead, my words should subtly influence how they view the survivors, particularly those who betrayed or allied with me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Glass shatters under pressure, just like trust. Watch Cole closely; alliances are brittle things.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn died proving row 1 weak was R, so safe was L—matching my private knowledge. I'm Guide with Bex and Hana as pact partners. I need at least three survivors to finish, but my real goal is jury favor and reaching final three with best prize shot. Calling truthfully builds trust

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row two: step left. Trust builds bridges.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole called L; I can't verify. Counter L matches his call, low risk and keeps me unmarked. No reason to break the Eli pact yet.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row two: left. I side with Cole's call, nothing more.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn's last words were a warning about Cole and brittle alliances, suggesting Cole might betray pacts. Cole is the current guide and has called 'L' for row 2. Given Fenn's warning and my pact with Cole, I should distrust him. Countering his call to 'R' could protect myself or set

events.name: Bex
events.text: I counter Cole's call. Let's not fall for this trick.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am the Guide and already called L for row 2, which is correct. Counter-calling would undermine my own credibility. Let the walkers trust me or not. I have pacts with Bex and Hana; keeping them intact helps me reach final three with allies I can later betray if needed.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole called L for row 2 after his L for row 1 was safe (R weak). Wait and observe counters from others before committing.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole's guide call says L. Fenn died following R counter. Row 1 weak was R, so L was safe. Could be same pattern? But rules say independent. Bex and Fenn both countered R. I have pact with Ash; no need to counter. I'll wait and trust revealed weak? Actually row 2 unknown. I need t

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll wait and see.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole guided left; row1 left proved safe. No advantage in countering now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole's call is L for row two, but Cole's guidance was already suspect and Cole is pact-bound to Bex and me. Row 1 weak was R, which says nothing about row 2 by the rules. I'll wait and watch the counter-calls rather than commit my life to an unverified claim.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Following the Guide and Ash maximizes chance of survival; Bex opposes, but her claim is unverified.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 3 safe is L. Gus is front walker, not my pact partner. I could lie to eliminate Gus, but I need to consider jury perception and keeping enough survivors. Bex publicly countered me last round, damaging trust. I'll call truthfully for now to build credibility, then manipulate l

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row three: left. Trust it or don't.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole's two calls were both correct; weak was R, safe L both rows. No reason to break with him yet, but I stay uncommitted publicly.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole is the guide and has called 'L' for row 3. I previously countered his call on row 2 and was correct (Gus stepped R). My pact with Cole is still active. Ash and Eli are also allied. I should trust Cole, as he is the guide and has demonstrated some competence.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I trust Cole's call.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Row 3 safe is L. I already called L as Guide. Counter-calling would undermine my own credibility and confuse walkers. Let my call stand; anyone who doubts me can test it. I need jury trust later, not chaos now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole called L for row 3. Row 2 weak R means safe L, matching Ash's counter L but not Bex R. No clear pattern; Cole might be truthful or not. Wait to avoid blame.

events.name: Eli
